subject: اللغة الإنجليزية
lesson: Parts of speech Top Tip, vocabulary matching and sentences
outcomes: Identify a word's part of speech before choosing its meaning
Match eight tourism words with their meanings and use them in sentences

tf.why: Many adverbs end in -ly, like steadily.

tf.s: 'Architecture' means the design of a building.
tf.why: Architecture is about how buildings are designed.

tf.s: 'Flock' as a verb means to go somewhere in large numbers.
tf.why: For example: tourists flock to the beach in summer.

tf.s: A meaning can match a headword even if it is a different part of speech.
tf.why: The meaning must be the same part of speech as the headword.

tf.s: 'Draw' can mean 'attract', as in 'The festival draws many tourists.'

tf.why: 'Variety' is a noun: a variety of goods.

tf.s: When 'major' is a noun, it can mean an army officer.
tf.why: That is why you check the part of speech of the headword first.

tf.s: Adjectives describe actions, and verbs describe nouns.
tf.why: Adjectives describe nouns; verbs show actions.

tf.s: Checking the part of speech helps you eliminate wrong options.
tf.why: Options with a different part of speech can be removed.
'Steadily' means in a regular, gradual way.

boxes.q: Which part of speech describes a noun?
boxes.why: Adjectives describe nouns, e.g. a major city.
Architecture is a thing, so it is a noun.
Architecture is the design of buildings.
People flock to places in big crowds.

boxes.q: Complete: 'The souq sells a ___ of goods.'
boxes.why: A variety of goods means many different kinds.
'Major' describes a noun, e.g. a major city.

boxes.q: Which word is usually an adverb?
boxes.why: The -ly ending often shows an adverb.

boxes.q: What should you check first in the Top Tip?
boxes.why: Find the part of speech, then match the meaning.
Verbs show actions, like flock or draw.

hunt.q: Word: go somewhere in big numbers
Word ending often seen in adverbs

mcq.q: Which of these words is a noun?
mcq.why: Architecture names a thing, so it is a noun.

mcq.q: In the Top Tip, what do you do with options that are a different part of speech from the headword?
mcq.why: Removing them leaves only the possible meanings.

mcq.q: Which list contains four parts of speech?
mcq.why: These are the four main parts of speech studied in the lesson.

mcq.q: Which word means 'the design of a building'?
Choose the best word: 'Every winter, tourists ___ to the beaches of Salalah and Muscat.'
mcq.why: We need a verb meaning 'go in large numbers'.

mcq.q: Choose the best word: 'The number of visitors has grown ___ every year.'
mcq.why: We need an adverb to describe how the number grew.

mcq.q: Which sentence uses 'draw' in the sense of 'attract'?
o: The new museum draws thousands of visitors.
Please draw a map of your town.
He draws pictures in his book.
Draw a circle on the board.

mcq.q: The headword 'major' is an adjective. Why is 'an army officer' a wrong meaning here?
o: It is a noun meaning, not an adjective meaning
mcq.why: The meaning must be the same part of speech as the headword.

mcq.q: Why must the meaning be the same part of speech as the headword?
o: Words of different parts of speech cannot replace each other
mcq.why: A correct meaning can replace the word in a sentence.

mcq.q: In 'The souq sells a variety of goods', which part of speech is 'variety' and how do you know?
o: A noun, because it comes after 'a'
A verb, because it shows action
An adverb, because it ends in -y
mcq.why: Words after 'a' or 'the' are often nouns.
